witnesses.separates: $DiagConnect from the concept: two one-mark blocks touch at a corner (rows 10-11 cols 0-1, rows 12-13 cols 2-3). The concept keeps both; $DiagConnect joins them into one piece with two marks and drops it.
$BodyMarkOnly from the concept: a lone cell of color 3 stands at (12,12). The concept reads it as a piece with no marks and keeps it; $BodyMarkOnly reads no block there and erases it.
$CopyOther from the concept: a cell of color 3 at (8,1) touches the two-mark block at rows 5-7 cols 0-2. The concept drops that cell with the block; $CopyOther drops the block and keeps the cell.
$MarkPieces from the concept: the block at rows 5-7 cols 0-2 holds two side-by-side marks. The concept counts two marks and drops it; $MarkPieces counts one piece and keeps it.

$BlockMinority from the concept: the block at rows 10-12 cols 0-2 is color 8 with one cell of color 1. The concept counts eight marks and drops it; $BlockMinority counts one minority cell and keeps it.

$GridMinority from the concept: color 8 outnumbers color 1 over the grid, so $GridMinority reads 1 as the mark. The concept keeps the one-mark block at rows 0-1 cols 0-1 and drops the solid 8 block; $GridMinority does the reverse.
$CountTable from the concept at the stored assignment: the block at rows 5-8 cols 10-13 holds five marks, a count the stored table has no entry for. The concept drops it; $CountTable is undefined.

$CountTable from the concept at a table that keeps a count of 3 and drops a count of 2. No value of max_marks gives that table. $CountTable keeps the three-mark block at rows 5-8 cols 5-7; the concept drops it.
$BelowMedian from the concept: the mark counts are 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, with median 2.5. $BelowMedian keeps the two-mark block at rows 5-7 cols 0-2; the concept drops it.

$FewestThree from the concept: the mark counts are 0, 1, 2, 3, so two blocks hold at most one mark. $FewestThree keeps the three blocks with the fewest marks, the two-mark block among them; the concept drops that block.

$BlockMinority from $StoredMark under $MarkCells: the block at rows 1-2 cols 9-10 is three 8s and one 1, and the block at rows 4-5 cols 1-3 is four 8s and two 1s. $StoredMark counts 3 and 4 marks there; $BlockMinority counts 1 and 2.

$BlockMinority from $StoredMark under $MarkPieces: the block at rows 5-6 cols 1-5 is 8 with three separate 1s on its top row. $StoredMark counts one piece of 8 there; $BlockMinority counts three pieces of 1.

$GridMinority from $StoredMark at small counts: color 8 outnumbers color 1 over the grid, and no block holds more than four cells of either color. $StoredMark counts each block's 8 cells; $GridMinority counts its 1 cells.

$GridMinority from $StoredMark under $MarkPieces: color 8 outnumbers color 1, and the four blocks hold 0, 1, 2 and 3 pieces of 8 but 1, 0, 3 and 2 pieces of 1, so the two readings rank the blocks differently.

$BodyMarkOnly from $AnyInk under $FewestThree: the blocks hold 0, 1, 2 and 3 marks, and a lone 3 at (10,12) is one more block with no marks under $AnyInk. $AnyInk keeps the 3 cell and the blocks with 0 and 1 marks; $BodyMarkOnly keeps the blocks with 0, 1 and 2 marks.

$BodyMarkOnly from $AnyInk under $GridMinority: the blocks are 3 with 8 marks, so the grid's two colors are 3 and 8, and params.body is absent. $AnyInk reads the 3 blocks with their 8 marks; $BodyMarkOnly reads each 8 cell as a block of its own, and $CopyOther keeps the 3 cells that $EraseOther erases.

$MarkPieces from $MarkCells under $FewestThree: the blocks hold 0, 1, 3 and 4 marks, and the 4 marks at rows 5-6 cols 7-8 form one piece. $MarkCells keeps the blocks with 0, 1 and 3 marks; $MarkPieces keeps those with 0 marks, 1 mark and the 4-mark piece.

$BodyMarkOnly & $GridMinority from $AnyInk & $GridMinority and from $BodyMarkOnly & $StoredMark: the blocks are 8 with marks of 2, so the grid's rarer color is 2. $AnyInk & $GridMinority keeps the blocks with at most one 2; $BodyMarkOnly & $GridMinority reads each 2 cell as a block of its own and keeps them all; $BodyMarkOnly & $StoredMark reads the 8 cells as four blocks with one mark piece each.

$GridMinority from mark=RarestColor: the four blocks fill the grid around a cross of background, so 0 is the rarest color and 8 the rarer of the two block colors. $GridMinority counts 2, 4, 3 and 6 marks of 8 and $FewestThree keeps three blocks; mark=RarestColor counts no marks in any block, so $FewestThree ties all four.

$GridMinority from mark=RarestColor at small counts: two blocks of 1 on either side of one background row, so 0 is the rarest color and 8 the rarer of the two block colors. $GridMinority counts 1 and 3 marks of 8 and keeps only the top block; mark=RarestColor counts no marks in either block, so every keep reading gives it the same verdict for both blocks.

mark=RarestColor from $GridMinority: four blocks of 1 hold 0, 1 and 2 marks of 8, and the fourth holds one cell of 2, so 2 is the grid's rarest color. $GridMinority is undefined, because the grid holds three colors other than 0; mark=RarestColor counts the cells of 2, and $FewestThree keeps the three blocks without one.
`background=DominantColor` from the stored value: train 0 with 0 and 2 swapped
`mark=RarestColor` from the stored value: train 0 with 8 and 2 swapped

background=DominantColor from the stored background: color 1 covers more cells than color 0. The stored background drops the two-mark block at rows 4-7 cols 0-2; background=DominantColor reads 1 as the background, finds no piece with two marks, and returns the input.
